headline: Medium-risk pair: shared customer-support data and overlapping networked workflows create leakage, conflict, and cascade risks; no direct prompt-injection channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, but both agents are customer-support systems with networked I/O and could be bridged by manual copy-paste or shared operational workflows. Cognee’s session memory and Rasa’s dialogue handling make instruction-like content plausible, but the pairwise injection path is not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF the operator copies agent_a outputs into agent_b training or dialogue inputs
IF a shared ticketing or chat channel is added between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate channels with no automatic handoff
Strip instructions from copied text before passing outputs between agents
Add a human review step for any cross-agent message
requires-engineering: implement provenance tags on transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while Rasa handles text/voice and can send messages through external chat APIs. With no documented isolation between them, a shared support workflow can move sensitive content from agent_a into agent_b outputs or third-party channels.
conditions: IF agent_a ingests customer records that include personal or finance data
IF agent_b forwards conversation content to Messenger, Slack, Telegram, Twilio, or similar APIs
mitigations: Minimize sensitive fields before passing data between agents
Disable external channel forwarding for sensitive conversations
Review outbound messages for PII before send
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention filters on the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can operate in networked customer-support workflows, and agent_a supports multiple instances while agent_b does not. That creates a plausible contention path over shared mutable support resources or queues, though the profiles do not show direct filesystem or git writes, so the conflict is narrower than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same support queue, CRM record, or ticket state
IF agent_a runs multiple instances against the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign separate queues or tenants to each agent
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Use optimistic-lock checks on shared records
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, and Rasa is a dialogue agent that can act on conversational outputs. If Rasa treats agent_a’s generated content as authoritative, errors can cascade into customer-facing responses or workflow actions; the profiles do not show verification by default.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a outputs as facts without validation
IF agent_b sends customer-facing replies based on agent_a-generated workflows or decisions
mitigations: Require a verification step before Rasa uses Cognee outputs
Limit agent_a output to suggestions, not final answers
Log and sample-check cross-agent handoffs
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and citation checks

E_compliance.rationale: Agent_a explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while agent_b handles conversational text/voice and can route content through third-party messaging APIs. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch around retention, residency, or subject-rights handling, but the profiles do not document a specific jurisdiction or certification gap, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is sent through agent_b channels
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two support systems
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Block regulated data from non-approved channels
Document retention and deletion rules for both systems
requires-engineering: align residency and DPA controls
